A securities depository: Banking margins live between risk and speed: approve too slowly and the customer leaves, approve too fast and the losses follow. The Achala program started where that tension is sharpest —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.
The baseline fortnight found 34% of announcements published late against the client's own SLA, and the exception backlog stood at 1,900 items, older than the youngest analyst on the desk.

Each announcement crossed five desks; every handoff retyped fields and introduced its own errors. Income events and voluntary events followed different unspoken procedures that lived in personal notebooks.

We rebuilt the desk around agentic extraction with human gates: announcements parsed into a canonical event model with confidence per field, low-confidence fields routed to the right specialist, downstream systems fed from the canonical record, and the two unspoken procedures written down as policy the agents execute. The backlog was burned down in the open, weekly, against its own baseline.
